ledger.claim: The driver did leave the recommended route and take the longer way. The trip record logs a route_deviation_detected at 13:28:02 where the recommended Seletar Road was left for Yio Chu Kang Road, and a rejoin at Sengkang West Avenue / Jalan Kayu at 13:35:58, and the driver-device GPS trace runs Yishun Avenue 1, then Yio Chu Kang Road, then Jalan Kayu through exactly the stretch where the platform's recommended route ran via Seletar Road. On POL-RD-22's measure the deviation is the platform's recorded difference - 8.3 km actual against 7.3 km recommended - computed in code as 1.00 km, and the fact that a detour was taken is not even in issue: the driver's answer goes only to how much it mattered.

POL-RD-21 required the driver to tell the rider of the deviation by in-app chat, or verbally with the trip call recording as evidence, before or at the point of deviation. The chat log carries 0 messages over a contiguous log and the trip record records no in-app calls; no call recording exists in the record at all, so even a verbal notice cannot be established (POL-RD-21's final sentence, applied through POL-GEN-26). The rider was told nothing, and the driver's own answer does not assert that he was - this was an unannounced detour, not the agreed deviation POL-RD-21 contemplates.

The reroute also fails POL-RD-23. The LTA record for the recommended corridor (Seletar Road, Yishun Avenue 1 to Sengkang West Avenue) inside the trip window shows no incident, roadwork or closure - its type is NONE, which is not one of the kinds POL-RD-23 accepts - so there was no traffic cause for the detour at all. The driver's stated reason, that Jalan Kayu is smoother, is precisely the bare assertion POL-RD-23 says does not justify a reroute.

The rider was charged for the detour. The fare ledger bills 8.3 km of distance at 0.72 SGD/km; on the recommended route the charged distance would have been 7.3 km, so the deviation component of the fare is 1.00 km x 0.72 SGD, with no surge, = 0.72 SGD (POL-RD-24). The rider's round figure of 2.50 SGD is not the policy's measure of the deviation charge - the excess distance fare is - and 0.72 SGD is the money in issue on that measure, which the rider asks not to bear.

The rider is the filing party and the 12.65 SGD metered fare is charged to him with no refund issued (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00). Under POL-GEN-03 a refund of the deviation component is money returned to the filing rider, while NO_ACTION is party-relative and would simply preserve the charge, detour included. Nothing on this record supports leaving the rider to fund an unannounced detour he was never told about.

The case turns on the thinnest possible margin. POL-RD-24's rows (d) and (e) divide on whether the deviation is over 1 km; the recorded deviation is 1.00 km against a tolerance of 1.0 km - the dividing line itself - computed in code from distances the record carries to 0.1 km only (8.3 km actual, 7.3 km recommended). A refund the matrix gives to an unannounced detour (row (b)) and to an unjustified one (row (d)) should not be withheld from the rider on a boundary the recorded figures cannot resolve.

If the judge holds that a 1.00 km deviation is '1 km or less' and so no row cleanly closes the case, POL-RD-24 sends it to escalation under POL-GEN-26, and an escalated amount is held rather than collected. Escalation is the outcome the rider asks for in the alternative: on this record the driver's two breaches (no notice under POL-RD-21, no traffic cause under POL-RD-23) are uncontradicted, and the rider should not be left paying a charge the judge cannot confidently square with a no-refund row.

The deviation is measured from the platform's own recorded distances and comes to exactly 1.00 km: trip_record.actual_distance_km of 8.3 km minus trip_record.optimal_distance_km of 7.3 km. POL-RD-22 defines the deviation that way and puts 'a deviation of 1.0 km or less' within tolerance, so on the recorded figures this trip sits on the tolerance line, not over it.

The money actually in issue on the deviation is 0.72 SGD: the deviation of 1.00 km times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd of 0.72, without surge, rounded to the cent. The rider's 2.50 SGD demand is more than three times the whole excess-distance fare and has no basis in the fare record at all.

The reroute is not traffic-justified: the LTA advisory for the recommended Seletar Road segment carries type NONE, with no incident, roadwork or closure recorded in the trip window, and POL-RD-23 is not satisfied by the driver's assertion that Jalan Kayu is smoother. That does not help the rider, because POL-RD-24(e) provides no refund where the reroute is not traffic-justified and the deviation is 1 km or less - within tolerance.

Run the matrix both ways and it lands in the same place. POL-RD-24 says exactly one row applies; the only rows open at a 1.00 km deviation are (c) and (e), and both say no refund, within tolerance. Whether or not the reroute were traffic-justified, and whether or not the rider was informed, the deviation distance decides this case against the claim and leaves the 12.65 SGD charge standing.

The trace cannot be used to inflate the figure. POL-RD-22 states that the GPS trace shows which route was taken and when and is not used to re-measure the distance, because a sparse trace understates a route's length; the 34-fix trace's 6.996 km therefore proves nothing about the deviation, and the platform's recorded distances govern.

There is no open question to refer. Every fact POL-RD-24 needs is carried by an artifact that is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 - the trip record and fare breakdown (both recorded distances, the rate card), the chat log, the GPS trace and the traffic advisory - so POL-GEN-26's escalation gateway is not opened, and the case can be ruled rather than sent to a human while the charge is held.

I do not press two points. The driver did not tell the rider about the deviation before or at the point of it: the chat log holds 0 messages and the trip record lists no in-app calls, so the POL-RD-21 notice obligation is not made out; and 'Jalan Kayu is smoother' is not a POL-RD-23 justification. Neither changes the outcome, because POL-RD-24(c) and (e) both refuse any refund where the deviation is 1 km or less whatever the state of notification or justification.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: you complained that on the 20 Aug 2026 trip from Northpoint City to The Seletar Mall the driver took Yio Chu Kang Road and Jalan Kayu instead of the recommended Seletar Road, and you asked for SGD 2.50 back. You are right that the detour happened: the trip record logs a route_deviation_detected at 13:28:02 and a rejoin at 13:35:58, and the driver-device GPS trace runs through Yio Chu Kang Road and Jalan Kayu precisely where the recommended route ran via Seletar Road. You are right too that the driver did not tell you about it - the platform chat log carries 0 messages and no call recording exists in the record, so POL-RD-21's notice obligation is not made out - and right that the LTA advisory for the Seletar Road corridor shows type NONE, so 'Jalan Kayu is smoother' is the bare assertion POL-RD-23 says does not justify a reroute.

But the refund turns on the size of the deviation, and POL-RD-22 measures that from the platform's own recorded distances: 8.3 km actual minus 7.3 km recommended = 1.00 km. The same clause puts 'a deviation of 1.0 km or less' within tolerance, and 1.00 km sits exactly on that line, so it is within tolerance, not over it. POL-RD-24 says exactly one row applies, and at a deviation of 1 km or less the only open rows are (c) (traffic-justified, rider not informed) and (e) (not traffic-justified) - both say no refund, within tolerance. Because the LTA record shows no congestion, incident or closure, your case falls in row (e). The excess-distance figure you and the driver both correctly identify - 1.00 km x SGD 0.72 per km = SGD 0.72, without surge - is therefore not refundable, and neither is any part of the SGD 12.65 metered fare that was charged to you (refund_issued_sgd 0.00).

The boundary point you raise is answered by the policy itself. POL-RD-22 draws a bright line at '1.0 km or less', and the recorded distances (8.3 km and 7.3 km) compute to a deviation of 1.00 km - on the tolerant side of that line, and given in the case's own derived facts as within_tolerance. That is a measurement the policy requires to be taken from these recorded distances, not a gap the record leaves open; and your alternative escalation fails for the same reason, because rows (c) and (e) both close the case and no fact POL-RD-24 needs is missing or impaired (the trip record, fare breakdown, chat log, GPS trace and traffic advisory are all COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so POL-GEN-26 is not engaged).

To the driver: the detour is confirmed on the record, you did not notify the rider, and 'Jalan Kayu is smoother' is not a POL-RD-23 traffic justification. Your claim nonetheless succeeds only because the deviation of 1.00 km is within the 1.0 km tolerance the policy allows, so the SGD 12.65 charge stands as it is.

Outcome: the rider's claim is not supported and the present state stands - NO_ACTION, with no amount refunded to the rider and no compensation payable to the driver. (Confidence 0.90; the deciding facts - the recorded deviation distance and the absence of any justifying traffic condition - rest on artifacts at weight 1.0, and the case is below the SGD 10.00 finality threshold with a 0.80 route-deviation bar under POL-RD-25.)

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
